name: Clockodo
subcategory: team time tracking and legal working-hours records
tagline: German time tracking for teams: project timers, working-hours records, absences, and billable reports.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Time tracking is one of the most cloneable categories there is: a timer, a customer, a project, a service type, an hourly rate, and a sum. An agent can produce a local web app with start/stop timers, manual entry correction, weekly totals, and a CSV or PDF export in a single sitting, and it will genuinely cover a freelancer's needs. What it will not cover is the reason companies buy Clockodo, which is defensible records of employee working hours under German law plus payroll and accounting handoff. If you are one person billing a handful of clients, the SaaS is mostly paying for polish and mobile convenience. If you have employees, a works council, or a tax advisor who wants a specific export, stop reading.
coreLoopDIY: Start and stop timers against a customer, project, and service, correct entries by hand, then export billable hours per project as CSV with computed totals.
requirements: A browser you keep open, or a small always-on machine if you want it reachable from your phone
whatYouLose: Compliance-shaped working-hours records: audit trails, signed-off timesheets, overtime and break rules, the stuff a German labor audit actually asks for
Native iOS and Android apps with offline capture and a widget, which is where most real time entries get made
Accounting and payroll exports (DATEV, lexoffice, invoicing tools) that someone else maintains when the formats change
Multi-user reality: roles, approvals, absence and vacation accounting, manager reports
Automatic reminders when you forget to stop a timer, which you will
moatNotes: The moat is regulatory and organizational, not technical. None of it applies to a one-person build.
whyPeopleStillPay: Businesses do not pay Clockodo for a stopwatch, they pay it to be the system of record for what employees worked, in a form that survives a tax advisor, a payroll run, and a labor audit. That means maintained exports, roles and approvals, absence rules, and someone else's problem when the law or the DATEV format shifts. A solo freelancer gets almost none of that value and is mostly buying mobile apps and the fact that it already exists. The split is clean: if hours leave your computer and enter someone else's ledger, pay; if they only become a line on your own invoice, build.
notes: The clone is easy; remembering to hit stop is the actual product feature.
prompt:
Build a single-user, self-hosted time tracking web app. Local only.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js 15, App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, single file at ./data/time.db
- Drizzle ORM with a migration script
- No auth, no accounts, no cloud, no telemetry, no analytics

Data model:
- customers: id, name, archived
- projects: id, customerId, name, hourlyRate (cents, nullable), archived
- services: id, name (e.g. Development, Meeting, Support), billableByDefault
- entries: id, projectId, serviceId, startedAt, endedAt (nullable = running), note, billable

Features, in scope:
- Today view: one big start/stop control, pick customer, project, service, optional note. Only one timer may run at a time; starting a new one stops the current one.
- Entry list for the selected day with inline edit of start time, end time, note, and billable flag. Manual entry creation for forgotten work. Duration shown as HH:MM.
- Week view: grid of days by project with daily and weekly totals, plus a target hours per week setting to show over/under.
- Reports page: date range, filter by customer/project/service/billable, totals in hours and revenue using project hourlyRate.
- CSV export of the filtered report, one row per entry plus a totals row.
- Settings page: target hours per week, rounding rule for exports (none, 5 min, 15 min), currency symbol.
- Seed script with two customers, three projects, three services, and a week of sample entries.

Out of scope, do not build:
- Multi-user, roles, approvals, absence or vacation tracking
- Invoicing, DATEV or payroll exports
- Mobile apps or push notifications
- Any third-party API

Requirements:
- Timers must survive page reloads and server restarts: running state lives in the database, elapsed time is computed from startedAt.
- Store all timestamps as UTC ISO strings, render in the system timezone.
- Keyboard shortcut: space toggles the timer on the Today view.
- Any config goes in .env, read at startup, with a committed .env.example.
- README with setup, migrate, seed, dev, and build commands, plus one line on how to back up data/time.db.
